papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
papers.abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schrödinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.

papers.title: Discrete time crystals and heteroclinic switching in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers
papers.abstract: We investigate the mechanisms underlying the emergence of discrete time crystals in actively mode-locked semiconductor lasers. Our analysis is based on a Haus master equation generalized to retain carrier memory between round-trips. We perform a detailed bifurcation analysis that reveals a well-defined hierarchy of subharmonic states, illustrating how pulses may suppress their neighbors when the modulation runs faster than the pulse round-trip frequency. To identify the underlying mechanism, we derive effective equations of motion that couple the pulse energies, their positions relative to the modulation transmission maxima, and the local time-dependent gain. These reveal that transitions between time-crystalline states occur via transcritical global bifurcations, opening a regime of heteroclinic winnerless competition between symmetry-degenerate configurations.

papers.title: Quantifying the importance of equation of state and transport property compatibility in supercritical fluids
papers.abstract: High-fidelity simulation of supercritical flows requires accurate values of thermodynamic properties including the density (rho), specific heat cp, enthalpy h, and entropy s as well as transport properties such as the viscosity (eta) and thermal conductivity (lambda) as functions of the temperature T and pressure P. In simulations of mixtures, such as supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) with contaminants, a generalized equation of state (EoS) is often used, leading to errors in rho(T,P) when compared to results from correlations developed specifically for individual species. Similarly, generalized correlations for eta and lambda are often used, with a corresponding decrease in accuracy. However, a second source of error is introduced in calculations of transport properties. These correlations are created and computed as functions of T and rho instead of as functions of T and P. Because of this, when eta(T,rho )and lambda(T,rho) are calculated, errors in rho(T,P) propagate through the calculation. This work creates a procedure for tracking both errors caused by using a generalized correlation for eta(T,rho) and lambda(T,rho), and for tracking the errors caused by using a generalized correlation for rho(T,P) in these calculations. The viscosity and thermal conductivity of supercritical CO2, N2, andCH4 are used as examples to demonstrate how to separate the errors due to the generalized property correlations and the errors due to the generalized EoS. Both sources of error are largest near the critical temperature Tc. These errors are large enough to impact both the numeric stability and the accuracy of simulations.

papers.title: Time-gated optical-parametric-amplification and field-resolved detection of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals
papers.abstract: Infrared spectroscopy is a key tool to study complex structural dynamics in molecular systems. However, resolving weak or broad vibrational modes is challenging due to their rapid decay. Here, we demonstrate a technique to significantly extend the detectable lifetime - and thereby spectral resolution - of molecular signatures by employing synchronized time-gated optical parametric amplification of mid-infrared free-induction decay signals. Utilizing a Cr:ZnS laser system and a nonlinear ZnGeP2 crystal, we achieve a 10-fold increase in the electric field strength of the infrared molecular signal, yielding a two-orders of magnitude enhancement in dynamic range and a 2-fold increase in the signal-to-noise ratio. Using isopropyl alcohol as a model system, we demonstrate that OPA-enhanced detection extends the observable window of vibrational modes up to 72 %. This approach allows for the reconstruction of high-fidelity molecular fingerprints that resolve complex vibrational relaxation pathways and weak structural dynamics, previously hidden within the background and noise, providing a pathway for new high-sensitivity and time-resolved studies of complex chemical structures.

papers.title: Bathyspheres, dust devils, lunar plumes and Martian drones: a generalised mathematical model for particle-fluid flow fields generated by static particle bed entrainment across macroscopic scales
papers.abstract: We consider a recently derived mathematical model for the mechanism by which a wind driven flow entrains particles into a fluid from an otherwise static particle bed, a process that is fundamental in initiating and driving the phenomenon of particle cloud formation. This model was previously applied to the "helicopter brownout" problem, in which, as a helicopter descends towards a bed of sand, the downwash and swirling flow from the rotors entrain particles into the air, forming a high-velocity particle-laden cloud around the helicopter. Here, we define a new measure of particle cloud formation potential, outline how the model can be incorporated into existing Computational Fluid Dynamics software, and extend the model to scenarios including: formation of particle clouds in the absence of swirl, such as those caused by a bathysphere descending to the ocean bed, or a rocket landing on the lunar surface, in which case we can precisely predict the critical height above the surface at which particle cloud formation is initiated; generation of dust clouds by less powerful downwash and swirling flows caused by drones or other smaller rotorcraft, such as NASA's Ingenuity Mars helicopter, in which case gravitational effects are included in the model; formation of dust devils (dust clouds formed within and around an upwardly circulating columnar air flow), in which case downwash is replaced by updraft. In each case, predictive models are derived through minor adaptations to key modelling assumptions.

papers.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
papers.abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects. Programmable couplers and optical delays reshape known single-photon temporal waveforms through coherent interference between time bins. Conversion to a common single-bin mode concentrates amplitudes from $N$ bins in $\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ mixing stages, simultaneously improving temporal indistinguishability and freeing channel time. Simulations yield mode overlaps above 99.9\% for exponential and Gaussian inputs. For $N=256$ and $0.5\,\mathrm{dB}$ loss per stage, STC gives a 45.6-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate than temporal gating at equal mode overlap for two exponential inputs. Relative to long pulses, the shortened temporal matched mode can support an approximately 41-fold higher photon-pair coincidence rate when the available time-multiplexing capacity is fully utilized.

papers.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
papers.abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

papers.title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.

papers.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
papers.abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.

papers.title: Vertically-coupled microring resonators for lithium niobate on insulator integrated photonics
papers.abstract: We propose and demonstrate lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) microring resonators that are verticallycoupled to index-matched silicon-rich silicon nitride (SiN x ) access waveguides as an alternative to conventional lateral coupling schemes for integrated photonics applications. The wafer-scalable fabrication process involves a planarization step exploiting a single-step and reproducible spin-coating of a SU-8 epoxy spacer layer which allows a controlled separation to be established between the resonator and its access waveguide. The resulting multimode and single-mode microring resonators exhibit, for their fundamental TE 0 mode, intrinsic quality factors of 4.0 x 10 5 and 3.4 x 10 5 , respectively.

papers.title: Magnon-polaritons in terahertz resonators based on antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism
papers.abstract: Terahertz magnon-polaritons in antiferromagnets with weak ferromagnetism are theoretically investigated using YFeO$_3$ as an example. Dispersion relations are obtained for the quasi-ferromagnetic and quasi-antiferromagnetic modes. It is shown that the intrinsic Fabry--Perot resonances of the magnetic slab provide strong coupling, but their low quality factor limits the cooperativity. The photonic crystal cavity increases the cooperativity of the quasi-antiferromagnetic mode from $C\sim6$ to $C\sim41$ at 300K and to $2.2\times10^3$ at 63K.

papers.title: Inversion symmetry breaking by interlayer hybridization in a tetralayer van der Waals heterostructure
papers.abstract: Inversion symmetry breaking unlocks a broad range of physical phenomena fundamental for modern technologies, motivating efforts to engineer noncentrosymmetric materials. In this context, monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides, which naturally lack inversion symmetry, have emerged as a versatile platform for valley physics, strong excitonic effects, and nonlinear optics. However, in their hexagonal stacking phase, inversion symmetry is restored in even-layer stacks and bulk form, suppressing these effects and limiting applications. In this work, inversion symmetry breaking is demonstrated in a vertically stacked tetralayer heterostructure assembled from two intrinsically centrosymmetric bilayer flakes, as evidenced by second harmonic generation measurements with an intensity comparable to that of their constituent monolayer. Spectroscopic measurements and theoretical estimations indicate that effective symmetry breaking in the tetralayer heterostructure is driven by interlayer hybridization, giving rise to pronounced electronic and phononic signatures. This symmetry breaking further induces polar anisotropy, with an intensity ratio reaching 2.36. We propose that asymmetric contributions from excitons to the second harmonic optical dipole may influence this behavior. These findings establish interlayer coupling as a critical mechanism for introducing inversion symmetry breaking and tuning the optical response of van der Waals heterostructures, providing a powerful strategy for photonics and optoelectronics in two-dimensional materials.

papers.title: Radiation-driven melting and porous flow in the near-surface layer of an ice sheet
papers.abstract: The ablation area of an ice sheet can undergo melting both directly at the surface and in the metre or so below the surface, due to the penetration and absorption of shortwave radiation. The fate of the meltwater has important implications for the mass balance of the ice sheet; some of it runs off into surface streams and eventually to the ocean, while some is stored in the porous `weathering crust', and can refreeze. We present a fluid-mechanical model to analyse the downward percolation and lateral drainage of the meltwater in the crust, and its influence on porosity, saturation, temperature and melting rate. Previous models have either ignored the possibility for lateral drainage, in which case the crust is always saturated with water, or have made ad-hoc assumptions about where and how the meltwater runs off. Through a series of analytical and numerical solutions to the model, we find that lateral drainage has the effect of controlling the water table within the weathering crust, which separates an unsaturated region near the surface from a saturated aquifer beneath. Under fluctuating weather conditions that induce melting and refreezing, the lateral drainage can result in the near-surface ice being more porous and also colder than is the case without lateral drainage. The model is able to predict the partitioning of the meltwater between surface and subsurface runoff, and refreezing, and has potential to be incorporated within larger-scale models of the ice-sheet mass balance.

papers.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
papers.abstract: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.

papers.title: Turbulent wakes behind nine bluff-body shapes from direct numerical simulation and particle image velocimetry
papers.abstract: We present a cross-validated dataset of turbulent wakes behind nine bluff bodies at Reynolds number Re = 10,000: a circular cylinder, a 2:1 elliptical cylinder at 0° and 90°, short and long isosceles triangles with the apex upstream or downstream, and a square cylinder at 0° and 45°. Each body was studied by wall-resolved direct numerical simulation (DNS) with a spectral-element solver and by time-resolved planar particle image velocimetry (PIV) in the MIT Intelligent Towing Tank. The DNS records contain time- and spanwise-averaged velocity, pressure and Reynolds stresses, 24-bin phase-averaged fields keyed to the lift signal, drag and lift histories, and one three-dimensional instantaneous snapshot per body; the PIV records contain the matching time-mean and phase-averaged fields in the same coordinate frame. The DNS set-up is verified against reference cylinder data at Re = 3900, and DNS and PIV at Re = 10,000 are compared field by field. The dataset supports the development and testing of data-driven turbulence closures, reduced-order models, and wake-stability analyses across geometries with distinct separation behavior.

papers.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
papers.abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.

papers.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows. We introduce TurtLES, a 14 TB dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes in the shear-layer transition regime, computed via high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations. The dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with 3-11 million points per frame, spanning variations in geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack. Unlike existing datasets, TurtLES combines (i) physically realistic turbulence with an active energy cascade driven by vortex stretching, (ii) dense irregular meshes, and (iii) long-horizon temporal dynamics. We benchmark state-of-the-art neural operators on autoregressive rollouts and identify key failure modes, including temporal instability, loss of small-scale energy, and challenges in learning on large irregular domains. TurtLES provides a new benchmark for evaluating surrogate models on 3D turbulent wakes at industrially relevant mesh resolution.

papers.title: Mode interaction in inclined-layer convection: a physical interpretation
papers.abstract: We carry out a numerical investigation of the Oberbeck--Boussinesq equations in a fluid layer inclined against gravity. Equilibria containing different numbers of co-rotating rolls are computed. Mixed-mode branches connect branches containing states with four and six identical co-rotating rolls. These branches display two contrasting routes to reducing (or increasing) the number of rolls, one in which rolls disappear (or appear) and another route in which rolls merge (or split). These results are interpreted in light of the $(2,3)$ mode interaction scenario.

papers.title: Selection versus residuals: deep-learning solvers for the Dubreil-Jacotin-Long equation and application to mode-2 internal solitary waves
papers.abstract: Neural solvers offer structural flexibility for the Dubreil-Jacotin--Long (DJL) equation of internal solitary waves, which also admits the trivial state, oscillatory wavetrains and broadened near-solutions. A solver must select the physical wave before resolving it. Turkington's variational principle selects the wave through the nonlinearity of the available potential energy (APE). An exact virial partition shows that every localized wave carries more kinetic energy than APE, so a quadratic APE would favour a broadened field. The nonlinear APE enhancement, $1.27$--$2.06\times$ for the computed waves, reverses this ordering, although the preferred width remains weakly selected. From a shared KdV-derived start, a constrained Deep Ritz objective recovers the mode-1 wave, whereas strong- and weak-form residual objectives, which vanish at every exact solution and therefore do not favour the physical wave over other roots, lose the prescribed APE within one descent round. The recovered wave is under-resolved because its residual is dominated by high-wavenumber error that the energy barely penalizes, and a residual refinement at exact APE then meets every acceptance criterion. Structurally excluding mode 1 from the trial space, we compute mode-2 waves on four stratifications. A computed wave core qualitatively reproduces the two-lobe structure observed on the South China Sea shelf. In the deep basin, the selected core misses the residual criterion, and residual refinement widens it with little change in the energy objective. The two resolved linear estimates suggest weaker relative mode-1 radiation at larger ratios of wave half-width to resonant wavelength.

papers.title: A hair-thin implant opens the entire depth of the mouse brain to revisiting the same structures at subcellular resolution
papers.abstract: Ultrathin multimode-fibre endoscopes provide minimally invasive access to subcellular structures throughout the depth of the mouse brain. Here we introduce a chronically implantable interface with a diameter of 144 μm, about the thickness of a human hair, that extends this capability to longitudinal imaging, enabling repeated access to the same fine structures over extended periods. The system supports weeks-long tracking of individual dendritic spines, allowing quantitative comparison of their dynamics and survival across dendritic compartments. We further demonstrate longitudinal intracellular calcium imaging during spontaneous and stimulus-evoked activity in the same cells across days, as well as repeated measurements of blood flow in the same vessels across multiple brain regions. This chronic endomicroscopic platform provides stable, minimally invasive optical access for longitudinal subcellular-resolution imaging of brain structure, activity and blood flow across depth.

papers.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
papers.abstract: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers. Measurements reveal two robust spectral features, a broad maximum near 1000 nm and an epsilon-near-zero peak near 1350 nm, that persist across wide variations in material and excitation parameters. Hydrodynamic-Maxwell simulations identify an interface-specific convective mechanism activated by freeelectron density and effective-mass discontinuities at the oxide-metal boundary. As electronic homogenization develops across the bilayer, the response evolves toward one described by conventional Coulomb, Lorentz, and leading convective terms. These results establish second harmonic generation as a sensitive probe of interface-driven nonlinearities and suggest a broader role for electronic discontinuities in shaping nonlinear optical processes at surface and buried material interfaces.

papers.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
papers.abstract: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.

papers.title: TwinLight: A Multi-Timescale Physical-Layer-Aware T-API-Compliant Optical Domain Controller Digital Twin
papers.abstract: We demonstrate TwinLight, an open-source optical-network digital twin acting as an optical domain controller. Its T-API REST and telemetry streaming interfaces expose a physical-layer engine that combines a GNPy steady-state baseline with four analytical transients.

papers.title: Stable, High-Charge, Laser-Driven VHEE Beams for Preclinical Applications
papers.abstract: Laser-driven plasma accelerators (LPAs) are promising sources of very-high-energy-electron (VHEE) beams for medical applications, but increasing charge per pulse while maintaining pointing stability remains challenging. We demonstrate laser-accelerated beams with total charge per pulse reaching (559 $\pm$ 56) pC using an 80 TW laser system. The spectra have a dominant component at 40-60 MeV and a high-energy tail extending to approximately 200 MeV. Pointing jitter measured in air at the irradiation target plane reaches as low as 0.7 mrad. The beams were used for VHEE irradiation experiments involving a 10 mm region of interest through a 40 mm depth at 400 $\pm$ 20 mGy/pulse. Spectral reproducibility is quantified over fixed-setting shot sequences. Particle-in-cell simulations produce a peak-and-tail spectrum through acceleration in successive bubbles associated with a strongly modified plasma wake, providing a plausible mechanism for maintaining substantial accelerated charge despite strong beam loading. Dose-weighted time-of-flight calculations indicate an effective pulse dose rate of $10^{12}$ Gy/s and average dose rates of tens of Gy/min. These results establish an LPA operating regime relevant to preclinical VHEE irradiation.

papers.title: Complex Hyperspin Machine and Symmetry Quenching: Benchmark and scaling up to millions of degrees of freedom
papers.abstract: Driven-dissipative oscillator networks have been proposed to simulate spin models on physical hardware, mostly focusing on systems of binary (Ising) spins, or systems of spin vectors in low dimensions. The equalized hyperspin machine was recently introduced to provide a single platform to simulate general models of $N$ coupled spin vectors with tunable dimension $D$, realizing dynamical annealing protocols to vary the spin dimensionality in time. These schemes are limited to real spins coupled via real coupling matrices. We propose a generalization of the hyperspin machine that works with complex fields and deals with complex Hermitian coupling matrices, implementing an amplitude equalization scheme. This system, which we name complex hyperspin machine, can work on optimization problems with complex valued hyperspins that can be cast on complex $D$-vector Hamiltonians. We benchmark the machine against a differential evolution (DE) algorithm on complex $D=2$ hyperspins up to $N=80$, showing that the fraction of instances where a lower-energy solution is found grows with system size and coupling density, reaching $92.5\%$ at the largest considered sizes. When the DE finds a lower-energy solution, the machine still reaches a median relative energy deviation that lies between $10^{-15}$ and $10^{-12}$ while running at substantially lower computational cost. Using the complex nature of the field, we introduce a new dimensional reduction protocol that we name symmetry quenching, which collapses complex variables that map to XY spins onto real Ising spins by switching on the parametric pump. We show on Max-Cut instances with known ground states that symmetry quenching outperforms a fixed-pump Ising machine, reaching exact ground states in the presence of equalization. We scale the system to $N=10^6$ hyperspins, or $8\times10^6$ dynamical variables, on a Hermitian sparse two-dimensional lattice.

papers.title: Absolute Calibration of a Broadband Transmission Grating Spectrometer from 5 to 400 nm with Uncertainty Estimates
papers.abstract: We present the absolute calibration of a transmission grating spectrometer (TGS) with uncertainty estimates in the 5--400 nm range using synchrotron radiation at the BEAR beamline at Elettra light source in Trieste, Italy. Firstly, the spectral responsivity of a Si photodiode in the spectrometer was absolutely calibrated with respect to the absolutely-calibrated beamline photodiode. Subsequently, this photodiode was used to calibrate the transmittance of Zr and Al thin-film filters, along with bulk MgF$_2$ and UV-grade fused silica windows at their operating positions in the spectrometer to minimize mounting-induced uncertainties. Next, the quantum efficiency of the spectrometer's CCD camera was calibrated over the 5--400 nm range. Lastly, three gratings with line densities of 10000, 3000, and 1000 lines/mm were calibrated for spectroscopy in the ranges extending from soft X-ray to extreme-, vacuum- and deep-ultraviolet (DUV) wavelengths, respectively. The combination of various filters and gratings enables absolutely calibrated spectroscopy with high versatility across a broad wavelength range from soft X-rays to DUV.

papers.title: Redetermination of the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BaMgF4
papers.abstract: BaMgF4 (BMF) has the potential to serve as a platform material for vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) nonlinear optics owing to its ferroelectricity and high UV transparency down to 130 nm. However, the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients reported for BMF span approximately one order of magnitude, hindering a reliable assessment of its potential for nonlinear optical applications. Here, we redetermined these coefficients by combining Maker fringe, wedge, and single-pass second-harmonic-generation measurements at a fundamental wavelength of 1064 nm. Our results establish that all the second-order nonlinear optical coefficients of BMF lie in the range of 0.01-0.04 pm/V. We determined d31 to be 0.035 pm/V, which is among the largest coefficients of BMF, while it has been underestimated relative to the other coefficients in previous studies. Although d31 is not the largest coefficient, the use of its long corresponding coherence length is beneficial for quasi-phase matching, particularly for VUV generation, where the fabrication of lower-order quasi-phase-matching structures is crucial.

papers.title: When is an Optical Design Problem a Mass Transfer Problem?
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. An optical problem is specified by a function defining a particular family of supporting surfaces for the optical element. We introduce the notion of geometric equivalence between optical and transport problems, which is directly related to the possibility of formulating an optical design problem as a mass transfer problem. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. For these problems, the necessary condition is shown to fail in physically admissible configurations. We also study an optical element with a single working surface and an arbitrary regular incident wavefront. In the far field, geometric equivalence to a mass transfer problem requires a planar or spherical wavefront, whereas in the near field with a planar target, the necessary condition fails for an arbitrary smooth wavefront.

papers.title: Low-Rank Iteration for Efficient Calculations of Topological Surface States
papers.abstract: Surface states are hallmarks of topological phases, and their efficient computation is crucial for topology characterization. Conventional supercell methods (SCM) approximate semi-infinite systems as finite periodic ones, but suffer from high computational cost, artificial inter-surface coupling, and slow convergence near band edges. Recently, boundary problems for semi-infinite systems have been recast as block-tridiagonal equations and solved by the cyclic reduction method (CRM) and the transfer matrix method (TMM). However, these approaches remain resource-intensive, as fine-mesh discretization produces very large matrices. Recognizing the intrinsic sparsity and low rank of these matrices, we develop a low-rank iterative method (LIM) with stochastic trace estimation that substantially reduces complexity and memory without sacrificing accuracy, while remaining straightforwardly parallelizable. Benchmarks on 2D and 3D topological systems show orders-of-magnitude acceleration over CRM and TMM. LIM extends readily to heterostructures, defective interfaces, and non-Hermitian systems, providing an efficient platform for topological and plasmonic surface phenomena.

papers.title: An acousto-optic colorimeter for color psychophysics
papers.abstract: A complete model of human color perception requires the ability to present any color as a stimulus.Most existing measurements were collected with physical color samples, and current laboratory generators, such as displays and multi-primary LED systems, work with a small number of fixed primaries. Published color-difference data therefore cover about 40\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram, while commercial wide-gamut displays already reach two thirds of it and need difference metrics there. We describe an acousto-optic colorimeter that lets the experimenter choose the primaries. The device selects up to four narrow bands from a supercontinuum (white-light) laser, each with electronically set wavelength and intensity, and covers 95\% of the CIE~$xy$ chromaticity diagram. Threshold-scale color differences, presented in alternation as in a discrimination experiment, are reproduced with a mean error of 0.08--0.12 CIEDE2000 units ($ΔE_{00}$) at five CIE-recommended color centers. Because one color can be built from many combinations of narrow bands, the bands are chosen for the task: the finest adjustment for color matching, the least disagreement between observers for color-difference measurement. In simulations with 151~individual observers from a published dataset, with these bands observers see colors 0.6--1.9~$ΔE_{00}$ from the intended one on average, against 1.2--2.5~$ΔE_{00}$ on a calibrated wide-gamut LCD, lower at every center. The approach applies to any narrowband source and lets experimenters use saturated colors while limiting the effect of individual differences in color vision.

papers.title: Influence of Flow on Discharge Behaviors and CO2 Conversion in Gliding Arc Discharges
papers.abstract: Plasma reactors present themselves as a unique means of electrified chemical production, particularly in the conversion of greenhouse gases (e.g., CO2) back into chemical feedstocks. Warm plasmas, such as gliding arc discharges, represent a growing class of catalyst-free plasma reactors that demonstrate high energy efficiency and scalability. Here, we introduce mean discharge time as a characteristic descriptor of gliding arc dynamics, extracted directly from voltage and current waveforms. Electrical signatures for distinct plasma behaviors (modes) were established using high-speed photography, and discharge time distributions were evaluated as a function of Reynolds number. Mean discharge time is shown to decrease non-linearly with Reynolds number, providing a link between arc behavior and underlying fluid dynamics, which is otherwise neglected in traditional reactor characterization. Mean discharge time thereby provides a quantitative, operando descriptor of transient gliding arc dynamics and stability, offering insight into discharge behavior that traditional characterization approaches do not capture.

papers.title: Anisotropic Thermalization in Far-from-Equilibrium Flows
papers.abstract: We present a deterministic discontinuous Galerkin (DG) finite-element solution of the Boltzmann equation, without moment-closure approximations, under a class of far-from-equilibrium deformations. Specifically, we consider affine flows which reduce the Boltzmann equation to a purely velocity-space problem for the reduced distribution function in a reduced velocity field. We solve the reduced equation using a tensor-product Lagrange DG discretization for four representative flows: simple shear, pressure shear, bi-directional shear, and a vortex flow. Our principal finding is that the velocity distribution is well-approximated by an anisotropic Gaussian throughout the evolution, despite the non-equilibrium conditions. Further, we show the evolution of the covariance tensor of the Gaussian distribution is equal to the inverse of the right Cauchy-Green tensor in the free-streaming limit without collisions. This prediction compares very well with the numerical solution at short times; at longer times, they grow apart, reflecting the influence of particle collisions.

papers.title: Variational Parameter Calibration with Physics-Aware Latent-Space Surrogates
papers.abstract: Forward and inverse modeling of parametric dynamical systems requires surrogate models that are not only accurate for state prediction, but also informative for parameter calibration. However, a systematic end-to-end differentiable formulation for coupling deep-learning-based reduced-order surrogates with variational parameter estimation remains underdeveloped. In this work, we introduce a physics-aware neural-network-based latent-space framework for reduced-order forward modeling and variational parameter estimation. The proposed autoencoder-based approach yields a differentiable surrogate that maps physical parameters to predicted flow fields through a latent representation. The observable supervision is used during offline training to encourage the latent variables to retain information correlated with system parameters, while the online inverse problem is solved in the parameter space through the surrogate-induced observation operator. The method is evaluated on two computational-fluid-dynamics benchmarks. The results show that reconstruction accuracy alone is insufficient for inverse modeling, owing to the lack of end-to-end differentiability or physics awareness for variational parameter calibration. Quantitative latent-space analysis further shows that observable supervision improves case-level separability and temporal organization of latent representations. Experiments with realistic measurement settings, including noisy, low-resolution, randomly masked, and block-wise partial observations, demonstrate the robustness of the proposed framework and show that it generally reduces calibration error and variability compared with the standard surrogate models.

papers.title: Few-cycle electro-optic light on thin-film lithium niobate
papers.abstract: The twin fields of ultrafast optics and nonlinear photonics enable applications ranging from attosecond science [1, 2] and ultrafast electronics [3] to molecular spectroscopy [4, 5], nonlinear optics [6-8], quantum nanophotonics [9] and precision metrology [10]. However, bringing these capabilities-including ultrashort pulse generation, dispersion control, and strong nonlinear interactions-together within a scalable photonic integrated platform requires exceptional performance and cooperation between components while preserving sufficient optical power across the circuit. Here we demonstrate an integrated multi-functional nonlinear photonic system that transforms continuous-wave (CW) light into high-peak-power femtosecond pulses and harnesses them for pulse-driven nonlinear optics on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN). Microwave-driven electro-optic (EO) broadening followed by integrated dispersive compression generates 230-fs Fourier-transform-limited pulses with energies up to 3.3 pJ at 30.7 GHz, representing orders of magnitude higher pulse energy than previous integrated pulse synthesis at comparable repetition rates [11]. In a 0.3-meter dispersion-engineered TFLN waveguide, soliton dynamics compress the pulses to 35 fs (6.7 optical cycles), accompanied by coherent spectral broadening exceeding 330 nm. In a fully-monolithic architecture, EO synthesis, dispersive compression and a high-Q nonlinear resonator are integrated on a single TFLN chip, enabling resonantly-enhanced pulse pumping and coherent spectral broadening at pulse energies as low as 400 fJ. By unifying microwave-controlled pulse synthesis and pulse-driven nonlinear interactions, our work establishes a direct path from CW excitation to few-cycle nonlinear optics on chip, with opportunities spanning microwave photonics [12], optical frequency synthesis and metrology, and mid-infrared and terahertz generation [13, 14].

papers.title: Emergent Space, Time, and Lorentz Symmetry from Binary Sequences
papers.abstract: We construct an information theory framework in which the fundamental objects are binary sequences of length $n$, equipped with the bitwise XOR operation. The only physical observables are counts of XOR-generated symbol classes, while the exact locations of symbols are inaccessible. Averaging over those locations ultimately yields the Minkowski interval as an invariant object that maximizes (information) entropy. Correlations between two binary sequences are base-4 sequences that we label as ``events'', and events are connected with maps. The entire kinematic structure of Special Relativity is recovered under minimal assumptions, i.e. counts that represent space and time increments carry equal informational weight. The central claim is that Lorentz symmetry is the typical large-n behaviour of XOR counting. At finite $n$ the framework yields a discrete rapidity spectrum, a bound $γ_{\max} = O(\sqrt{n})$, and interval fluctuations of relative size $O(n^{-1/2})$, with standard special relativity recovered as $n \to \infty$. However, the light cone and one null coordinate are exact for every microscopic configuration, so the symmetry group is undeformed and dispersion relations are unmodified. Thus, the theory, though discrete, implies no Lorentz violation of the standard phenomenological kind. Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays already require $n \gtrsim 10^{23}$; interferometry excludes the variant in which $n$ scales linearly with system size, leaving a holographic area law. The most striking prediction of the framework concerns systems at the maximum of their information capacity, where $n$ is necessarily finite: black holes and de Sitter space. There the corrections are of order one within a Planck proper length of the horizon, regardless of the horizon's size, and the spacetime description fails altogether at the endpoint of black-hole evaporation, where $n$ itself is of order unity.

papers.title: Floquet Green's functions for lattice electrons driven by Gaussian quantum light
papers.abstract: We formulate Floquet Green's functions for noninteracting single-band lattice electrons driven by a reservoir-stabilized single-mode Gaussian quantum light source. The source is prescribed externally and is not updated by the many-electron polarization, while an active electronic probe still conditions the source evolution through the Peierls coupling. The two time arguments of a Green's function share one source history: the lesser and greater components are obtained by convolving a shared-history four-endpoint kernel with the continuous bath kernels before the final source trace, while the bath canonical anticommutation relation yields an equal-time covariance that seeds the retarded and advanced one-leg propagations. The Peierls coupling is treated nonperturbatively within the prescribed-source model, and classical Floquet theory is recovered in the appropriate limit. Numerical calculations on a minimal one-dimensional model show finite-coupling quantum-source corrections beyond a prescribed classical drive, together with spectral reconstruction and occupancy redistribution for squeezed vacuum and squeezed coherent sources. The squeezing parameter and phase provide additional control knobs, beyond classical amplitude modulation, for both sideband structure and occupied weight. This work provides a theoretical framework for quantum Floquet engineering of condensed matter with an externally prescribed quantum light source.

papers.title: Impact of strain and dark states on spectroscopic measurements of silicon-vacancy centers in diamond
papers.abstract: Negatively charged silicon-vacancy (SiV$^-$) centers in diamond offer an attractive platform for the development of many forms of quantum technology. However, questions remain in connection to how large ensembles of SiV$^-$ centers behave in concert. Here, we develop a computational model designed to simulate recent experiments where optical multidimensional coherent spectroscopy (MDCS) was used to examine a high-concentration sample of SiV$^-$ centers in diamond, revealing significant variations in spectral signature depending on the detection scheme. Simulation results reveal that strain effects are highly random in this system, with a characteristic axial strain of $2.8 \times 10^{-4}$ and a shear strain of $3.5 \times 10^{-5}$. They suggest in addition that highly strained centers (with values exceeding $1.5 \times 10^{-5}$) may become significantly decoupled from optical emission. The results have implications for the use of SiV$^-$ centers as quantum sensors.

papers.title: High-dimensional Supermode Photonics Enabled by Hierarchical Supersymmetric Transformation
papers.abstract: Modes provide a fundamental degree of freedom for photonic information processing, yet conventional multimode waveguides exhibit non-equidistant effective-index distributions, making closely spaced modes vulnerable to intermodal crosstalk. Supermode photonics can overcome this limitation by geometrically engineering coupled waveguide arrays to realize large and equidistant effective-index spacing, but precise supermode excitation and detection remain challenging at the subwavelength scale. Here, we report a hierarchical second-order discrete supersymmetric (DSUSY) transformation method that enables high-purity excitation and extraction of arbitrary target supermodes in a compact and scalable architecture. We experimentally demonstrate six-supermode multiplexing systems on silicon-on-insulator and silicon nitride platforms. Benefiting from the large supermode index spacing and the isospectrality of DSUSY transformations, the fabricated devices exhibit low insertion losses (<2.6 dB) and intermodal crosstalk (<-11.1 dB) for all channels over a 100-nm wavelength range. A high-speed transmission experiment on the silicon device achieves an aggregate data rate of 1.2 Tbit/s, with all channel bit error rates below the 7% hard-decision forward-error-correction threshold. The method can further support polarization-insensitive architectures, enabling compact polarization-supermode hybrid multiplexing. This work provides a scalable route toward high-dimensional supermode photonics for high-capacity optical interconnects, highly parallel AI optical computing, and high-dimensional quantum information processing.

papers.title: Observational constraints on Barrow holographic dark energy coupled with a non-cold dark matter component from DESI DR2
papers.abstract: We investigate the cosmological viability of Barrow holographic dark energy in a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker universe in which the dark matter component is allowed to have a non-zero pressure, characterized by a constant equation-of-state parameter $w_{m}$. By considering the future event horizon as the infrared cutoff, we derive the master equation, which describes the cosmological dynamics for the background space. We constrain the model against late-time data, combining the baryon acoustic oscillation from DESI DR2 with three different catalogues for the Type Ia Supernova measurements and the Cosmic Chronometers. The dark matter equation of state is constrained to $w_{m}=0.033_{-0.030}^{+0.045}$, $0.009_{-0.041}^{+0.047}$, and $0.033_{-0.029}^{+0.042}$, for the PantheonPlus, the Union3.0 and the DES-Dovekie supernova datasets respectively. Therefore, the pressureless limit is recovered within the $2σ$ regime. On the other hand, the Barrow exponent is weakly constrained, due to the $Δ-w_{m}$ degeneracy. The dark energy equation of state remains above the phantom divide throughout the redshift range probed. Finally, in the comparison of the statistical parameters with that of $Λ$CDM, it follows $Δ\mathrm{AIC}=+2.23$, $+0.75$, and $+1.38$, $\ $while for the Bayesian evidence we find $Δ\ln Z=-0.63$, $+0.47$, and $-0.13$, which suggest that the datasets considered in this analysis do not have a preferred model. Finally the relation with the corresponding Tsalis holographic dark energy model is discussed.

papers.title: Singularities in Soft Matter Systems
papers.abstract: When a liquid thread pinches off, its neck thins as it separates into two unconnected regions. Using continuum mechanics, we can predict that the neck reaches zero radius in finite time while its curvature grows without bound. Together, the vanishing neck and diverging curvature form a finite-time singularity. However, a real fluid does not realise these mathematical limits as molecular or material physics takes over once the neck becomes sufficiently small. Similar singularities arise throughout soft matter whenever a smooth continuum description is used at vanishing length scales. This review asks what the shrinking region forgets, what it retains, and which material length, time, or stress cuts off the apparent divergence. The dynamics near a singularity often become self-similar, with profiles at different times collapsing onto one shape when rescaled by the shrinking local length. Sometimes that collapse is universal enough that the surrounding geometry and forcing no longer determine the local dynamics. Nonetheless, the measured output could still depend on how the shrinking region is fed by the surrounding flow and on the small-scale physics that finally replaces the ideal divergence. Complex fluids and active matter change the same local balance by bringing their own timescales into the shrinking region. Beyond interfaces, the same logic applies when the localised object is a stress concentration or a defect in geometry or order rather than a moving surface. Singularities matter because they show where continuum theory stops being the relevant description and how the small-scale cutoff sets the outputs that count in printing, coating, aerosols, and stretchable solids.

papers.title: Non-resonant laser-driven narrowing of particle velocity distributions
papers.abstract: Stark acceleration and deceleration based techniques for generating particle ensembles with low velocity spread are useful in many experimental applications. For a given velocity distribution of a particle ensemble, these techniques accelerate or decelerate a small subset of the total population, with a low velocity uncertainty. However, narrowing the original velocity distribution by accelerating or decelerating the ensemble particles near the mean velocity is fundamentally limited and not yet explored. We present a numerical study of particle dynamics using neutral cesium atoms as an example. We investigate different interaction regimes, identify key limitations, and propose an interaction regime in which optical Stark deceleration can be used to narrow the velocity distribution of a propagating ensemble about its mean velocity. These findings have potential implications for optical manipulation and control, controlled collisions, and matter interferometry.

papers.title: Plasmonic Fourier Surfaces Revisited: Relating Bandgaps with Bound States in the Continuum
papers.abstract: Periodically corrugated metal interfaces supporting surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) belong to the earliest nanoplasmonic platforms. Even simplest reliefs described by a few harmonics - plasmonic Fourier surfaces - display markedly different far-field signatures depending on the corrugation depth and symmetry: shallow reliefs exhibit a plasmonic bandgap (PBG) between two hybridized SPP standing waves, while deeper reliefs support asymmetry-induced single sharp resonances, termed over the last decade as quasi-bound states in the continuum (qBICs). Although these spectral features have long been observed experimentally and treated empirically, the underlying eigenmode evolution connecting the shallow and deep corrugation regimes has remained largely unexplored. Here we revisit this long-standing problem by analyzing it in terms of modern eigenstate formalism. Starting from the Rayleigh hypothesis, we develop a concise first-principle analytical description that explicitly captures how one eigenmode transforms from a dark bound state into an observable qBIC, while the other turns from bright into an overcoupled, unobservable state - thus unifying the SPP manifestations featuring PBG and qBIC within the same eigenmode framework. Finally, we demonstrate the practical relevance of the theory by showing how precise eigenstate engineering can enhance the SPP refractive index sensitivity.

papers.title: Couette-Taylor instabilities in the small gap regime: the very counter-rotating case
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Couette-Taylor instability of a viscous fluid between two rotating cylinders in the small-gap, slow rescaled rotation rate, high Reynolds number regime, focusing on the very counter-rotating case $μ< μ_c \approx -0.8$ where the primary instability is non-axisymmetric. Starting from the Navier-Stokes equations, we derive a limit system that captures the leading-order dynamics and compute the critical Taylor number $T_c(μ)$ together with the critical axial and azimuthal wavenumbers. Near criticality, the weakly nonlinear behaviour is governed by a system of two coupled complex Ginzburg-Landau equations. All coefficients of this amplitude system including the cubic nonlinear terms are evaluated numerically from the linearised eigenfunctions and the associated adjoint problem. The reduced equations admit helicoidal waves (travelling in both the axial and azimuthal directions) and ribbon waves (standing axially, travelling azimuthally), and their existence and stability criteria are discussed. We also examine more exotic spatially modulated solutions that satisfy a third-order dynamical system, whose complete classification remains an open challenge.

papers.title: Boosting self hybridized exciton polaritons with metal clad WS2 waveguides
papers.abstract: The formation of Fabry Perot and guided wave self hybridized exciton polaritons in two dimensional materials results in long range exciton energy transfer and strong exciton exciton interactions. Here, we demonstrate that the coupling strength between photonic modes and excitons is significantly boosted by embedding the active excitonic layer in a metal clad WS2 waveguide. The photonic modes in this waveguide exhibit modified dispersion properties for both Fabry Perot type and guided wave exciton polaritons compared to pure WS2 flakes, and show an increased couplingr strength. Our results provide a robust approach for controlling exciton photon interactions and their coupling strength in hybrid heterostructures.

papers.title: Inelastic spreading of viscoelastic drops
papers.abstract: When a liquid drop impacts a solid surface, rebound and splashing are known to be suppressed by additives that induce elastic effects; however, the influence of elasticity on the maximum spreading radius remains debated. The difficulty lies in isolating elastic resistance from the enhanced spreading caused by viscous shear thinning. Here, we experimentally decouple these effects by investigating Boger fluid drops (constant-viscosity solutions with high elasticity) of polyethylene oxide (PEO) and polyacrylamide (PAAM). We demonstrate that elastic properties do not alter the maximum spreading ratio, even at high concentrations up to 1000 ppm. We formulate an energy balance that accounts for the inertial, capillary, viscous, and elastic contributions, and yields a dimensionless criterion ($Γ$) that estimates the degree of elastic effects. We show that $Γ\ll 1$ for all impact conditions tested, demonstrating that elastic effects are energetically negligible during droplet spreading, opposite to what Weissenberg and Deborah numbers would predict.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning for separation control in turbulent wind-tunnel flow
papers.abstract: This work investigates Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) as a tool for model-free closed-loop active separation control in a fully turbulent wind tunnel flow over a one-sided diffuser. The agent controls an array of magnetic valves (on/off) that eject compressed air into the boundary layer, while the environmental state is reduced to the signal from a single wall-shear-stress sensor placed near the natural transitory detachment point. The control law is learned in real time using Proximal Policy Optimization. Compared to the standard learning design based on the weighted sum of all rewards following an action, we demonstrate that a horizon aligned with the convective time of the flow leads to faster convergence and a more robust control strategy. The resulting control law corresponds to a low-duty-cycle actuation pattern that yields a forward-flow fraction of approximately $53\%$. This compares favorably with conventional and optimized periodic open-loop control ($\sim 40\%$ and $\sim 51\%$, respectively). The findings of this article indicate that, when embedded into an online experiment, DRL represents an efficient tool to identify robust and interpretable active separation control strategies.

papers.title: Optical-Memory Transport Imaging: A Transport-History Framework for Finite-Memory Tracers
papers.abstract: Finite-memory optical tracers encode upstream transport histories rather than instantaneous local flow velocities. We introduce optical-memory transport (OMT) imaging, a framework in which finite memory couples internal-state relaxation to transport through memory kernels. Under structured illumination, these histories are converted into measurable complex spatial-frequency response, whose local transfer-function limit yields constant-velocity inversion. Fisher-information analysis establishes kernel-dependent information limits and design principles for finite-memory transport imaging.

papers.title: Rf beam steering using on-ohip optical true time delay on 3 micrometer siliocn on insulator platfrom
papers.abstract: We present the design, packaging, and system-level experimental demonstration of a reconfigurable 5-bit, 4-channel optical true time delay (OTTD) chip realized on a 3 micrometer thick silicon on insulator (SOI) platform at VTT. The chip enables 32 discrete delay states over a 0 to 101 picoseconds range, with a delay resolution of 3.25 picoseconds, making it well suited for broadband RF beamforming with upcoming 6G FR3 band systems around 10 GHz. Each channel incorporates five binary weighted delay stages controlled by Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) based thermo-optic switches with an extinction ratio exceeding 25 decibels and an average switching power of 25 milliwatts. The chip is embedded within an analog radio-over-fibre (A-RoF) link, and the outputs are connected to a PCB-based four-element patch antenna array. Accurate RF beam steering is demonstrated at broadside and at 30 degrees from broadside using a 16 - QAM signal modulated at 100 MBaud on a 10 GHz carrier. An error vector magnitude (EVM) degradation of approximately 1 percent is observed upon steering, and an extinction ratio exceeding 50 decibels is measured between the two receiver positions. The results confirm the potential of integrated OTTD technology for compact, power-efficient, and broadband beamforming in next-generation wireless and radar systems.

papers.title: Quantum Theory of Third-harmonic Generation in Epsilon-Near-Zero Materials
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical framework, based on the Green's tensor quantization method, to describe third-harmonic generation in epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) materials and derive analytical, closed-form solutions for the generation efficiency. We validate our model against experimental measurements of wavelength- and angle-resolved third-harmonic generation efficiency from 30 nm-thin ITO nanolayers at low pump intensity, described under the undepleted pump approximation. Our results provide a local and scalar effective model for quantum nonlinear processes in dispersive and lossy ENZ media, and establishes a simple and reliable framework for investigating a variety of nonlinear optical phenomena with applications to quantum sensing, quantum information, and quantum nondemolition measurements.

papers.title: Revealing time characteristics of optical excitations in dielectric and plasmonic structures through cathodoluminescence interferometry
papers.abstract: Cathodoluminescence (CL) spectroscopy provides access to optical excitations with nanometer spatial resolution, but direct time-resolved measurements of optical resonances remain challenging. Here, we demonstrate that CL interferometry provides access to the temporal response, phase behavior, and modal spectral structure of resonant nanoscale scatterers without requiring ultrafast pump-probe schemes. We develop an analytical framework in which Fourier transformation angle- and frequency-resolved CL interferograms yields the decay time of optical resonances governed by the linear optical response. Multimode resonators exhibit characteristic temporal CL beating signatures associated with spectral mode splitting. By exploiting transition radiation emitted from a nearby metallic surface as a broadband reference, we further demonstrate phase retrieval and cross-correlation measurements between instantaneous and resonant emission processes. Experimental measurements on Au nanoparticles, broadband plasmonic emitters, Au nanostars, and Si nanospheres supporting multipolar Mie resonances confirm the theoretical predictions, and decay times in the range 1-10 fs are derived for each system. Our results establish CL interferometry as a powerful approach for accessing spectral, spatial, and phase information within a single nanoscale measurement with fs resolution.

papers.title: Stability of Orbital Angular Momentum Modes in Conventional and Ring-Core Optical Fibers
papers.abstract: Modal dynamics in multimode optical fibers are fundamentally governed by the inter- play between phase matching and intermodal coupling. In this work, we investigate the fundamental coupling mechanisms in ring-core fibers and identify a geometry-induced cou- pling suppression that significantly reduces coupling coefficients between orbital angular momentum modes compared to conventional multimode step-index fibers. This mechanism provides a clear physical explanation for the superior transmission stability of orbital angular momentum modes in ring-core fibers and establishes specific geometric constraints for the design of ring-core fiber-based mode converters.

papers.title: Strong, Mode-Selective Evxciton-Photon Coupling Driven by Polariton Scattering in the Mo2 Complexes at Ambient Conditions
papers.abstract: Quadruply bonded Mo2 complexes provide a distinctive molecular platform in which multiple two-level electronic transitions interact with quantized scattering modes under ambient conditions. Here we show that, in the Mo2 complexes, the intrinsic photonic modes selectively couple to molecular excitations, including the characteristic delta-delta(star), ligand to metal charge transfer (LMCT) and metal to ligand charge transfer (MLCT) transitions, to form the well-resolved exciton-photon hybrid states. By combining steady-state absorption, resonance fluorescence, and ultrafast transient spectroscopies, we identify distinct polaritonic branches associated with these electronic manifolds, with coupling strengths spanning the strong and ultrastrong regimes (g/omega0 up to 0.1). Mode-selective coupling accounts for the pronounced spectral reorganization for the singly oxidized complexes, including the emergence of absorption valleys and sidebands of the associated resonances in the steady-state spectra, characteristic polaritonic emissions in the photoluminescence spectra, and long-lived low-energy hybrid states in the transient spectra. These results support the picture that the Mo2 unit functions as an integrated molecular resonator whose intrinsic quantized field selectively drives and redistributes molecular excitations. This work strengthens the emerging view of bonded dimetal complexes as ambient-condition molecular quantum systems and provides a chemically defined platform for exploring polaritonic chemistry.

papers.title: Nanoscale graphitization and defect evolution in silicon-vacancy center-containing nanodiamonds under high-pressure high-temperature annealing
papers.abstract: Group-IV color centers, such as the silicon-vacancy (SiV) defect, are highly promising for solid-state quantum technologies. However, nanodiamonds typically exhibit significant lattice strain and structural disorder, which degrade their optical properties and hinder the resolution of the fine spectral structure at cryogenic temperatures. High-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) annealing offers a potential route to relax internal strain, although the phase stability of diamond at the nanoscale under such conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate the structural evolution of nanodiamonds during HPHT annealing using a Paris-Edinburgh press coupled with in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction at SOLEIL. A dedicated sample assembly combining nanodiamonds - NaCl - Pt enabled accurate pressure-temperature calibration and real-time monitoring of phase transformations. The diffraction data reveal that the onset of diamond-to-graphite transition occurs at approximately 1800 K at 2 GPa and 2120 K at 4 GPa under the applied HPHT heating protocol. These experimentally determined graphitization onsets define a practical pressure-temperature processing window for HPHT annealing of nanodiamonds while avoiding detectable graphitization and provide a calibrated framework for reliable off-beam annealing treatments that avoid graphitization. Photoluminescence measurements on samples annealed below the graphitization threshold show improved optical response, with partial resolution of the SiV fine structure at 12 K. These optical measurements suggest a relationship between nanoscale phase stability and the optical response of individual SiV-containing nanodiamonds following HPHT annealing. The experimentally established HPHT processing window provides a practical framework for the controlled processing of quantum nanodiamonds while avoiding graphitization.

papers.title: Evaluating the Role of Blockage Deficit Models in Robust Wind Farm Design
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in wind farm layout optimization regarding model choice and the impact of global blockage always exists. This paper evaluates these interactions by extending a multi-objective approach that maximizes mean Annual Energy Production (AEP) from a model ensemble while minimizing their variance. By incorporating the Self Similar blockage model into an ensemble of five wake models, we assess the impact of blockage physics on layout robustness. Results from a linear mixed-effects model indicate that including blockage leads to a non-significant average AEP reduction of 0.0624 GWh ($p$-value = 0.323). Conversely, it caused a highly statistically significant increase in uncertainty, with model disagreement rising by 0.177 GWh ($p$-value < 0.001). Additionally, computational runtime increased nearly nine times. These findings highlight an accuracy vs. certainty paradox, where theoretically necessary physics can compromise model consensus if implemented without re-calibration. Ultimately, this work suggests that simple blockage couplings act as a diagnostic for model incompatibility, emphasizing the necessity of careful model tuning for wind farm design.

papers.title: Direct experimental measurement of femtonewton-scale momentum transfer force from electron beams
papers.abstract: Electron beams (e-beams) are ubiquitous in imaging, patterning, and propulsion. This prevalence is rooted in the profound mastery of their wave-particle duality and energy-transfer pathways. Yet, a fundamental dimension remains largely unexplored: while the mechanical effect (i.e., the momentum transfer to a target) is theoretically known, quantification of its femtonewton-range force has remained elusive. This discrepancy represents a missing piece of the puzzle toward a comprehensive understanding of e-beam-matter interactions, and ultimately limits the multi-dimensional exploitation of e-beams. A force sensor combining femtonewton sensitivity, immunity to electromagnetic noise, compatibility with vacuum, and absolute calibration is critical to bridge the gap between theory and experiment. Here the FINEST (Femtonewton Interferometric Nanomechanical Electron-beam Sensing Technology) sensor is proposed and successfully tested to measure the force of an e-beam. FINEST is an optical-pressure-calibrated 3D spring-type optical sensor that operates reliably under e-beam conditions. Femtonewton-scale forces from 2-30 keV e-beams are directly measured, ranging from 505 fN to 13 pN. Both linear scaling with beam current and a non-monotonic energy dependence (peaking near 10 keV) are observed. Based on this calibrated force, the mechanical contribution to e-beam ice etching was quantitatively confirmed; its effect is orders of magnitude lower than the total etch depth and lacks noticeable energy dependence. By achieving the first direct experimental measurement of e-beam momentum transfer, this work adds a long-missing dimension to the physical landscape of e-beam processes. These findings provide a quantitative basis for furthering the multi-dimensional exploitation of e-beams, potentially transforming our approach to precision nanofabrication, sensing, and fundamental electron physics research.

papers.title: Dispersion Control of Chiral Exciton-Polariton Transport with Dielectric Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Exciton-polaritons provide a powerful platform for manipulating hybrid light-matter states with low effective masses and strong nonlinearities. Introducing chirality into these quasiparticles enables selective control over their spin and propagation, opening new opportunities for chiral transport and spin-selective polaritonic devices. We exploit the strong chiral light-matter coupling in silicon metasurfaces composed of tilted nanorod dimers to demonstrate selective transport of organic chiral exciton-polaritons. The metasurface supports surface lattice resonances and quasi-bound states in the continuum that simultaneously provide high photonic confinement and extrinsic chirality, giving rise to chiral exciton-polaritons in the achiral molecules. These exciton-polaritons exhibit a large magnitude of the dissymmetry factor, reaching a value of 0.93. Using photoluminescence Fourier microscopy and real-space imaging, we show that chiral exciton-polaritons propagate over distances exceeding 50 um without significant degradation of their dissymmetry, with characteristic propagation lengths of approximately 6-13 um. These propagation lengths correspond to an enhancement of 3 orders of magnitude compared to bare excitons. This work constitutes the first demonstration of enhanced and selective chiral transport of organic exciton-polaritons, driven by strong light-matter coupling, in achiral metasurfaces, paving the way for spin-selective polaritonic technologies using simple metasurfaces.

papers.title: Constraints on the Modified Emergent Dark Energy Model Using DESI DR2 BAO
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the modified emergent dark energy (MEDE) model using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 2 (DESI DR2), together with CMB information from the {\tt LoLLiPoP} (low-$\ell$) and {\tt HiLLiPoP} (high-$\ell$) likelihoods based on the latest Planck NPIPE PR4 release, Planck PR4 lensing, ACT DR6 lensing, and three Type Ia supernova samples (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, and Union3). We find that the MEDE model remains largely consistent with the standard $Λ$CDM cosmology. Although small departures from $Λ$CDM are allowed, the inclusion of SNe~Ia data drives the model parameters toward the standard cosmological scenario, with the parameter $α$ remaining consistent with $α=0$ at the $1σ$ level. The model does not significantly alleviate the $H_0$ or $S_8$ tensions: the inferred $H_0$ values remain below the SH0ES measurement, the sound horizon $r_d$ is nearly unchanged, and the predicted $S_8$ values remain close to those of $Λ$CDM. The reconstructed cosmological evolution closely follows the $Λ$CDM prediction, with deviations generally below the $0.5σ$ level. While the CMB + DESI DR2 dataset favors a full phantom regime, the inclusion of SNe~Ia shifts the evolution toward a full quintessence regime. Finally, although the $Δχ^2_{\rm MAP}$ and $Δ{\rm AIC}$ criteria indicate a marginally better fit than $Λ$CDM, the logarithmic Bayes factor provides only inconclusive evidence in favor of the MEDE model. Overall, the MEDE model remains compatible with current observations but does not exhibit the phantom-crossing behavior suggested by recent DESI DR2 analyses.

papers.title: Link-adaptive digital twin for robust physical-layer modeling in hybrid-amplified ultra-wideband optical networks
papers.abstract: Accurate physical-layer modeling is increasingly essential for reliable ultra-wideband operation and capacity optimization, especially under the intensified inter-channel stimulated Raman scattering (ISRS) effect. This paper proposes the link-adaptive digital twin (LA-DT) for hybrid-amplified ultra-wideband links to overcome the generalization and speed limitations of existing methods, achieving accurate modeling and robust generalized signal-to-noise ratio (GSNR) estimation across diverse links.
